summary: The 1909 wooden lookout and 1917 steel tower stood at a lower Hunter Mountain site until moved to the summit in 1950 or 1953; only footings remain there.

facts.design: 1909 wooden tower of timbers found on the summit; 1917 60-foot steel Aermotor LS-40 tower erected beside it
facts.status_note: Lower site only: the steel tower was re-erected on the summit (1950 per NHLR, 1953 per Wikipedia), where it now stands as us-ny-hunter-mountain; footings remain at the old site

access.note: Footings sit at a trail junction on the marked NYSDEC trail network; no source gives separate rules for the site.

visit.trail_note: Footings are at a trail junction where the tower stood (Wikipedia); the trails are marked NYSDEC blazed routes (NHLR).

events.note: Wooden tower built from timbers found at the mountaintop, about 40 feet below the true summit.
Steel 60-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower erected beside the wooden tower site.
Register says the tower was dismantled and re-erected on the summit in 1950; Wikipedia dates the move to 1953.

evidence.supports: 1909 wooden tower built from timbers found on the mountaintop
evidence.quote: Established in 1909 with a tower made of timbers found at the mountain top

evidence.supports: station about 40 feet below the true summit
evidence.quote: 40 feet shy of the true summit

evidence.supports: 1903 and 1908 droughts caused damage and led to calls for better fire control
evidence.quote: Severe fires during droughts in 1903 and 1908 caused thousands of dollars in damages and led to public calls for better fire control efforts.

evidence.supports: station one of the first facilities operated by Forest Fire Control
evidence.quote: This station is one of the first facilities operated by Forest Fire Control.

evidence.supports: 1917 60-foot steel Aermotor LS-40 tower erected beside the wooden tower
evidence.quote: In 1917 the present 60' steel Aermotor LS-40 tower was erected next to the wood tower site

evidence.supports: 1917 steel 60-foot (18.3 m) tower replaced the wooden one
evidence.quote: Eight years later it was replaced with a more permanent steel 60-foot (18.3 m) tower

evidence.supports: steel tower hauled in sections from Spruceton by horse team
evidence.quote: It was hauled in sections up the dirt road from Spruceton (now the Spruceton Trail) with a team of horses.

evidence.supports: register says tower dismantled and re-erected on the summit in 1950
evidence.quote: until in 1950 the tower was dismantled and re-erected at the current location on the summit

evidence.supports: Wikipedia dates the move to the summit to 1953
evidence.quote: In 1953, it and the cabin were moved one thousand feet (305 m) northwest along the ridge to the mountain's true summit

evidence.supports: footings of the original tower still visible at the trail junction where it stood
evidence.quote: footings of the original tower are still visible at the trail junction where it stood

evidence.supports: steel tower fully restored and open to the public
evidence.quote: The tower has been fully restored and is open to the public.

evidence.supports: volunteers staff the tower on weekends from Memorial through Columbus Day
evidence.quote: the tower has been staffed by volunteers of the Committee each weekend from Memorial through Columbus Day

evidence.supports: access by marked NYSDEC blazed trails
evidence.quote: Access is by clearly marked and well defined NYSDEC blazed trails

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the steel tower was dismantled and re-erected on the summit in 1950; Wikipedia says it was moved in 1953. The story reports both dates and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: This record is the same steel tower as us-ny-hunter-mountain, moved from the lower 4,000-ft site to the summit; consider linking the two records. The 1950 vs 1953 move date conflicts: us-ny-hunter-mountain uses 1950 without noting Wikipedia's 1953. The old-site footings rest on Wikipedia alone. NHLR has a 'Wood Tower 1909' photo caption but no usable license was found, so no photo was added.
